lawyer: Serajuddin Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.
parties:
Jaman Mia ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Zainab Bibi wife of Haji Abdus Salam ----- Opp.-Party
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff opposite party Jainab Bibi instituted Title Suit No. 236 of 1979 in the Third Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the defendant petitioner Juman Mia for his ejectment from the suit premises. It was stated that the tenancy commenced from the 1st Falgoon, 1362 B.S. The tenancy was admittedly for a manufacturing purpose The plaintiff opposite party served a notice upon the defendant petitioner u/s 106 of the Transfer of Property Act which was received by the petitioner on 17.6.76 (which was some time in Ashar, 1382 B.S.) asking him to quit the suit premises on the 31st Chaitra, 1382 B.S. In other words he was given 9 months' notice to vacate the suit premises. The suit was contested by the petitioner, among other points, on the question of the validity of the notice, but the suit was decreed by the learned Munsif. 

 In this application the only point urged by Mr. Serajuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner is that u/s 106 of theTransfer of Property Act the notice of termination of lease must expire "with the end of a year of the tenancy". The "end of a year of the tenancy" in the present case is the end of the month of Magh in any Bengali year. The plaintiff should have asked the defendant to vacate the suit premises at the end of Magh, 1382 B.S. since the tenancy admittedly commenced from the 1st Falgoon, But by requiring the defendant to vacate the suit premises at the end of Chaitra, 1382 B.S the expiry of the notice of termination has has not coincided with the expiry of the end of the year of the tenancy Hence the notice is bad and the suit ought not to have been decreed he submits. Mr. Ahmed has cited the case of Binoy Krishna Des Vs. Salsiceioni, 37 C. W.N. (P.C) 1 in support of his submission. 

 4. In the present case the plaintiff opposite party served the notice u/s 106 of the Transfer of the Property Act on 27.6.76 which was some time in the month of Ashar, 1382 B.S. She has given 9 months notice to the defendant petitioner to vacate the suit premises. As such the suit premise was used for manufacturing purpose the defendant petitioner was only entitled to 6 months' notice. The plaintiff opposite party could have asked the defendant petitioner to vacate the suit premises on the 31st Magh, 1382 B.S. and if she had done so it would have been a good compliance with the requirements of see 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. But she has given time in excess of the requirements of section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act and in such circumstances the requirements of section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act have been more than complied with. I am supported in my view by the decision in the case of Pannalal Biraji Vs. Kalyanmal, A.I.R. 1961 M.P.232, where it has been observed that section It 6, in the absence of a contract to the contrary the tenant is entitled to a notice for a period equal to half the length of the tenancy. Secondly, the tenant is also entitled, without prejudice to this right, to stay on till the end of a full month or a full year of the tenancy, as the case may be. If, the time given is in excess of the half term of the tenancy and the tenant is able to stay on for a half term before the date of the determination of the lease period (as in the present case), section 106 is complied with and in fact more than complied with though the notice terminates the tenancy on a date other than the one on which the lease term itself ends.
